We know that many of you are balancing your studies with work, caring responsibilities or other commitments, and we have tried to make the rules below as clear and fair as possible. If you have not yet received your login details, please contact the course office in your first week, as you will need them for almost everything described in this section. 4.1 Attendance Design is a practical subject, and much of what you learn will come from working alongside other students in the studio. For this reason, we ask that you attend at least 85% of all timetabled sessions, including workshops, studio days and tutorials. Attendance is taken at the start of every session using the sign-in sheet, so please arrive on time; if you arrive more than 15 minutes late, you will be marked as late, and three lates count as one absence. If you cannot attend a session, you must email your personal tutor before it starts, giving a brief reason. You do not need to provide a note for a single missed day. However, if you have three absences that were not reported in advance, you will be invited to a meeting with the course leader, Dr Chen Wei, to discuss how we can support you. Students whose attendance falls below 85% for the term may not be allowed to submit their final portfolio. 4.2 Deadlines and handing in work Your main piece of coursework this term is the design portfolio. It must be uploaded to the learning portal by 4 pm on 5 December. Paper copies are not accepted. The portal sends you a receipt by email when your upload is complete, and you should keep this as proof of submission. We strongly recommend uploading a day early, as the portal can be slow in the final hour before a deadline. Work handed in late will lose 5 marks for each day it is late, for up to three days. After that it will receive a mark of zero. If something outside your control, such as illness or a family emergency, stops you from meeting the deadline, you can request an extension using the extension form on the portal. Requests must be made at least 48 hours before the deadline, except in a genuine emergency, and must be approved by your personal tutor. Extensions are normally for up to one week. 4.3 Final presentation In the week beginning 12 January, every student gives a 10-minute presentation of their portfolio to a panel of two tutors, followed by five minutes of questions. Presentation slots are booked through the portal, and you must choose a slot by 20 November. Anyone who has not booked by then will be given a slot automatically, which may not be at a convenient time. You may bring printed boards or present from a laptop, but the room projector must be tested with a technician on the Friday before. 4.4 How your grade is worked out Your final grade is made up of two parts: the portfolio counts for 60% and the presentation for 40%. The pass mark for the course is 50. If you do not pass, you may resubmit your portfolio once, in March, but the mark for a resubmitted portfolio will be capped at 50. Grades are released on the portal about four weeks after the presentations, and every student receives written feedback from both panel members. 4.5 Peer feedback sessions Throughout the term there are four peer feedback sessions, in which small groups share work in progress and comment on each other's ideas. These sessions are compulsory and count towards your attendance. Past students have told us that these sessions were among the most useful parts of the course, and many have kept in touch with their groups long after finishing. A final word on wellbeing: the end of term can be a busy time, and it is easy to leave everything until the last week. Tutors are always happy to look at drafts during tutorials, and the college library runs quiet study evenings on Wednesdays. Please make use of them, and do not hesitate to ask for help early if you feel you are falling behind. If anything in this section is unclear, please speak to your personal tutor or to the course office, which is open from 9 am to 4 pm on weekdays. Updated versions of the handbook will always be posted on the portal.

Over the last eighteen months many of you took part in our hybrid working pilot, filled in surveys and joined the focus groups run by the People Team. Thank you. We had more than 300 responses, and they have shaped the policy below. Our leadership group signed it off last week, and it will apply to all staff from 6 January. A full copy is on the intranet; this message covers the main points. Before we get into the details, a little background. The pilot showed that most of you value the flexibility of working from home for focused work, but that teams missed the chance to meet in person, and new starters in particular found it harder to learn from colleagues. The policy tries to keep the best of both. It has been discussed with the staff forum and with each department head, and we have made several changes in response to their comments, including the extra support for home equipment described below. Time in the office Everyone is expected to work from the office at least two days a week. One of those days must be your team's anchor day, when the whole team is in together. For most teams this will be Tuesday, but some teams, such as Finance and Customer Support, will choose a different day because of their workload. Your line manager will confirm your team's anchor day by the end of this month. The second office day is up to you, as long as you agree it with your manager. If you would like to work a different pattern, for example three days in the office or a compressed week, please fill in the flexible working form on the intranet and send it to your line manager by 13 December. Requests to work fully remotely will still be considered, but these need to be approved by the People Team as well as your manager, and will usually only be agreed for specific roles or personal circumstances. Desks and booking We are moving to shared desks on both floors. From 6 January, there will be no fixed desks, and you will need to book a desk through the desk booking system at least 24 hours in advance. Lockers will be available for personal items and can be requested from reception. Please clear your current desk of all personal belongings by 20 December, when the cleaning team will start preparing the floors. Anything left after that date will be boxed up and taken to the post room. Core hours To make sure people can reach each other, everyone should be available between 10 am and 3 pm on working days, wherever they are working from. Outside these hours, you can arrange your day as suits you and your team. Please keep your calendar up to date so colleagues can see when you are in the office and when you are at home. Home working support Every member of staff working at least one day a week from home will receive a home working allowance of £25 a month, paid with your salary, to help with the cost of internet and heating. It will be paid automatically from the January payroll, so you do not need to apply. In addition, you can request one monitor, a keyboard and an office chair for use at home by completing the equipment request form. These remain company property and must be returned if you leave. Working from other locations Working from somewhere other than your home or the office, such as a holiday home or a family member's house, is fine for short periods. However, working from another country for more than 10 working days in a year needs approval from both your manager and the People Team, because of tax and insurance rules. Please ask well in advance. Reviewing the policy We know this is a big change, and we do not expect to get everything right straight away. We will run a short survey in June and review the policy after six months. Your feedback during the pilot was invaluable, and we want to keep hearing from you. Our director, Mohammed Aziz, will host an open question session on 10 December at 2 pm in the main meeting room and online, and all staff are welcome.
